_comment: Which labels, branches and gates Oneshot uses on its GitLab project. The project itself is NOT named here: GITLAB_REPO_URL in .env is the single source of truth for which project (host, path and API are derived from it), and the numeric project id is asked of GitLab when something needs it, never configured. Everything below must hold on whichever project that URL names — the labels must exist there and the branches must be protected there. `npm run doctor` checks only the branches against the live project; nothing checks the labels, so confirm them by hand on the project (see _comment_labels).
_comment_context: Read-only. Oneshot reads this repo for prior art and conventions; it NEVER writes to it, and hooks/write-scope.js denies every write under contextRepo for every phase. See docs/HOOKS.md 4.1. Skills/agents/rules are no longer sourced live from here: they are vendored into this repo's context/ (a committed snapshot of erp/.claude that also stays in GitLab), and SKILLS_ROOT (ONESHOT_SKILLS_ROOT) defaults to that vendored copy. skillsRoot below is informational only — nothing reads it — and records where the upstream skills live for a human syncing the snapshot.
_comment_labels: ONE label in, one label out. The exit label is 'Merged': the pipeline ends at the merge, so 'Ready For Deployment' would be a claim about a deploy nobody performed. The same edit that puts 'Merged' on puts labels.localTestsTrigger ('Ready for Automation Testing') on too, while the team has localTests.enabled: that label is what hands the merged ticket to the local automation tests, whose automation report is the last thing Oneshot posts (see _comment_localTests). Every label check is by NAME and is case-sensitive, so each name must match the project's label exactly and must already EXIST there: Oneshot never creates, renames or deletes a label, and a swap naming a label that is not there silently drops it. The ids are informational — nothing reads them. Verified on 2026-09-22 against the ERP project, which is the one GITLAB_REPO_URL names as this is written: 'Merged' (707) and 'In Review' (563) already existed there, and 'Loop' (1336) and 'Needs Human' (1337) were created that day, so the required pair is present. Pointing GITLAB_REPO_URL at another project means checking these names exist on it. There is no intermediate state machine — progress lives in the Slack card and the run journal, not on the board. 'review', 'testcaseReview', 'designReview' and 'notABug' are OPTIONAL; empty is the documented way to switch an optional LABEL off, and setting one to an existing label name switches it on. 'testcaseReview' is ON, naming 'TestCase Review' (1342), which was created on the project AFTER the move here — it was emptied on 2026-09-24 because ERP had no such label then, and that is no longer true. The others stay empty: 'Design Review' does not exist on the project, and 'Review' does exist but is deliberately left off because it is not board-only — it adds three human sign-off pauses. Empty switches off only the label, never the behaviour around it: an empty 'notABug' still lets bug reproduction stop a run (bugReproduction:false is what switches that off), it just adds no label when it does. 'review', when set, is never required and never swapped by Oneshot: a ticket carrying it alongside 'Loop' gets three extra human sign-off pauses (see README's 'Optional human review gates').
_comment_inReview: Added while a ticket's MR waits for a person to merge it, removed when the run finishes (merged) or blocks. Not the same as `review`, which is what makes a ticket need human sign-off. Empty or absent disables it.
_comment_localTests: The three labels of the local automation tests mode (src/localtests), which runs AFTER a ticket's change is merged and never inside the Loop. `localTestsTrigger` is what starts the mode, once one of the ticket's MRs is also merged into one of localTests.targetBranches (dev or stage): the Loop puts it on itself, in the same edit that puts on `exit`, whenever it merges a ticket while the team has localTests.enabled (mergeTriggerLabel), and a person can put it on any other merged ticket; a labelled ticket whose change is not merged yet waits quietly. `localTestsRunning` replaces it when QA approves a list with tests in it and the run starts. `localTestsDone` replaces either of them when the run is over — the automation report posted, passed or failed — or when QA approves going on with no local test at all. A run that could not happen (a setup error) puts `localTestsTrigger` back instead, so the ticket is picked up again. Exact, case-sensitive names that must already exist on the project, like every label here; doctor requires the trigger wherever merges put it on, and all three on a desk where localTests is on (see the localTests block). Verified on 2026-10-09 against arbisoft/erp, reading all 327 of its labels (two of these three sit past the first hundred, which is why listLabels pages): 'Ready for Automation Testing' (1354), 'Running TestCases Locally' (1352, renamed from 'TestCase Run Locally') and 'Automation Testing Done' (1355). Empty or absent switches the mode off, and with it the label at merge.
_comment_designReview: A SIXTH, OPTIONAL, board-only label, EMPTY (off) by default — set it to an existing project label to switch it on. Exactly the testcaseReview mechanism, for the design gate: added when that gate first posts its request, removed when it resolves, gating nothing itself. It is empty rather than pre-filled because a swap naming a label that is not on the project is silently dropped — so a default of 'Design Review' would look configured and do nothing. Note it is NOT the 'Design' label: that one is what puts a ticket through the design phase at all and is listed under preserveLabels.
_comment_testcaseReview: A FIFTH, OPTIONAL, board-only label, EMPTY (off) by default. swapLabel adds it the moment the testcases gate first posts its request comment (a QA sign-off is now pending) and removes it the moment that gate is approved -- see src/conductor/reviewgate.ts. It never gates anything itself and is never required alongside 'Loop'; its only job is letting a board view tell 'parked at testcases QA review' apart from every other parked/blocked reason. Empty string turns it off, same as leaving 'review' unset. Must exist on the project before relying on it, same rule as every other label here.
_comment_reviewAllRuns: TRUE = the review gates apply to EVERY run, not only tickets carrying the Review label or touching highScrutinyPaths. This is a deliberate change of posture: with it on, every run pauses after `plan` and after `testcases` for a human, and never merges its own MR. The one exception is a ticket the delivery-zone guard judges green (_comment_zones below): on this flag's account it is not asked after `plan` or `testcases` (the Review label and a guarded path still ask), and only the merge stays a person's. The path list still works and is still worth keeping — it is what makes a gate survive this being switched back off. The label trigger works only once labels.review names a label that exists on the project; it is empty in this config, so no ticket is gated by a label. Requires channels:history (or groups:history) on the Slack bot token; without it every gate sits 'pending' forever and every run parks, which is why doctor FAILS rather than warns while this is true.
_comment_bugReproduction: TRUE = before planning a fix, research reproduces a reported BUG on the base branch in the real app (skill: bug-reproduction). This is the project-wide switch, not the per-ticket one: a run only reproduces when the ticket ALSO carries the label mapped to bug-reproduction in config/phases.json (`Bug`), because bring-up and login are paid whether or not the ticket turns out to be a bug. An unlabelled ticket records 'not-applicable' and never starts the app. If the steps run and the correct behaviour is observed, the run PARKS on the Not a Bug gate: the evidence and screenshots are posted on the ticket and a QA reviewer from config/reviewers.json decides. Any other comment from them is feedback, and research reproduces again with it in its prompt. Only their `approved` stops the run: the entry label is removed, labels.notABug is added in its place WHEN ONE IS SET, and the evidence is posted as a ticket comment and in the Slack channel. labels.notABug is empty in this config, so the ticket is left with neither label and the verdict lives in that comment and the Slack post. Features, no-UI changes and anything that could not be run to the end (inconclusive) carry on as before. To overrule the verdict, add Loop back (and remove labels.notABug, if one was set): the run resumes at plan without reproducing again. A non-empty labels.notABug must exist on the project. FALSE switches the step off.
_comment_high_scrutiny: Paths the ERP's own .claude/rules/security.md marks 'escalate immediately'. A ticket whose PLAN or DIFF touches one gets the Review gates even without the Review label, because the label is human-applied and therefore forgettable — and the tickets most worth pausing on are exactly the ones nobody remembers to label. Matching is a plain substring test against repo-relative paths, so 'apps/payroll/' catches everything under it. The paths now live in config/risk-modules.json (the `paths` of every module) and are merged into this array at load. They gate review only: the Plane triage router no longer reads that file, it routes by the ERP repo's own .claude/zones.json. To disarm the path trigger, remove the module's `paths` in config/risk-modules.json — emptying this array alone does nothing. Add a one-off path here only if it has no module.
_comment_markers: Persistent labels Oneshot must copy through untouched on any label write. A label swap is one update_issue call carrying the full array, so anything not listed here and not the entry/exit label would be silently dropped.
_comment_zones: The delivery-zone guard (src/conductor/zoneguard.ts) is SWITCHED OFF: there is no `zones` block, so zoneGuardApplies() and refusedTicket() return false/null and no run is checked against a zone or refused for a label. Its only input, the ERP repo's .claude/zones.json, is not on ERP origin/dev yet (it arrives with arbisoft/erp!11060), and an enabled guard fails closed on a map it cannot read, so switching it on now would stop every AI ticket. To switch it on once `git -C "$WORK_REPO" show origin/dev:.claude/zones.json` succeeds, add this one line here: "zones": { "file": ".claude/zones.json", "guardLabel": "AI", "yellowLabel": "Zone: Yellow", "testsLabel": "Characterization Tests" }, and dry-run one AI ticket. With it on, an AI-labelled ticket whose plan or branch diff leaves green (or green+yellow on a ticket carrying yellowLabel) is blocked, red never runs, and a testsLabel ticket is refused before any phase. One that keeps to green, with no yellowLabel on it, is also not asked for plan or test-case approval under reviewAllRuns: it runs to its MR and waits there, labelled In Review, for a person to merge. yellowLabel is grooming's classification of the ticket, not proof its characterization tests merged: the release is Loop, which the pm-loop sweep adds only after the tests-only MR merges, and the guard trusts that rather than checking it. Remove the line to switch it off again.
_comment_branches: base is what ticket branches are cut from and what their MRs target. Do not infer it from the project's GitLab default branch, which need not be 'dev'. Everything in protected is refused by the git guard whatever the server would allow — which is why 'main' is listed even on a project that does not have it, or where it reports can_push=true for our token. doctor WARNs about a listed branch the project does not have, and FAILs one that exists but is not protected on GitLab: on a project with an unprotected 'main', protect it there or remove it from this list.
_comment_promotion: dev is FINAL. A ticket MR merges into base and the run is done — nothing is promoted onward. dev -> stage is deliberately absent rather than auto:false, because auto:false reads as 'a human owns this hop' (which is what it means for stage -> master) and that is not the reason here: the hop is switched off while the pipeline earns trust. With no entry whose `from` is the base branch, runPromotions() records no promotion and merge reports 'no automatic promotion applies to this base'. Restore by putting { from: dev, to: stage, auto: true } back — nothing else has to change, and note that config/deploy.json already ships dev (defaultRef), so the deploy never depended on this hop. stage -> master stays listed and stays manual: production release is a human act.

localTests._why: The local automation tests mode (src/localtests): the end of a ticket's pipeline. It runs AFTER a ticket's change is merged, never inside the Loop: the Loop's merge puts labels.localTestsTrigger on the ticket beside labels.exit, and a ticket carrying it whose merge request is merged into one of localTests.targetBranches (dev or stage) gets a throwaway ERP worktree at that MR's merge commit; the local-tests-scope session (onDemand, so the Loop never schedules it) picks the workstream-automation (Cypress) specs to run — the ones the change reaches plus the main-functionality (smoke) specs of every impacted module — and the list goes on the ticket for QA as the impacted-module report. A QA reviewer (config/reviewers.json qa) approves EVERY local run before it starts: `approved` runs it, `added <file>` adds a test file that is on the automation ref, `disapproved:` says what to change. Oneshot never writes or suggests a test. Once approved, scripts/localtests.cjs (plain code, no model) runs exactly that list on this desk against the merge commit on a throwaway copy of the automation database, posts the automation report, and marks the ticket labels.localTestsDone whether the tests passed or failed. This block is the team POLICY. `enabled: true` is also what makes every desk's merge put the trigger on. A desk RUNS the mode by pointing ONESHOT_LOCAL_TESTS_REPO in .env at its workstream-automation clone; left empty, that desk only adds the label at merge, and the desk that runs the mode picks the ticket up. `enabled: false` here switches the mode, and the label at merge, off on every desk. Read through localTestsConfig() (src/lib/config.ts), which treats any unusable field, and any of the three labels left empty, as off and says which one. The Cypress credentials never come from here: the run merges the desk's credentials file (ONESHOT_LOCAL_TESTS_CREDS) over the committed cypress.env.json into a mode-600 cypress.env.json in its throwaway state/runs/<iid>/wsa-run worktree, written before the app build and removed with that worktree at cleanup.
localTests._why_baselineDb: The Postgres database every run copies from (CREATE DATABASE <dbPrefix><iid>_<n> TEMPLATE <baselineDb>). No run ever writes to it. It must already exist on the desk with the automation data restored into it, and nothing may be connected to it while a copy is taken, because Postgres refuses a template that has sessions. A desk whose baseline has another name sets ONESHOT_LOCAL_TESTS_BASELINE_DB rather than editing this. A plain lower-case identifier only, because it is written into SQL.
localTests._why_pg: Where that Postgres listens. The per-run copies are created and dropped on this server, so it is the desk's own. pgUser empty means the libpq default (the OS user). ONESHOT_LOCAL_TESTS_PG_HOST, ONESHOT_LOCAL_TESTS_PG_PORT and ONESHOT_LOCAL_TESTS_PG_USER override these per desk.
localTests._why_dbPrefix: Every per-run copy is named <dbPrefix><iid>_<n>, so cleanup can find and drop leftovers by this prefix without touching any other database. A plain lower-case identifier, and never the start of baselineDb, or cleanup would match the baseline.
localTests._why_automationRef: The workstream-automation commit both throwaway worktrees are checked out at: the scope session's state/runs/<iid>/wsa, where the temporary changes are made, and the run's state/runs/<iid>/wsa-run, where they are applied again before Cypress runs.
localTests._why_allowedPaths: The only places in workstream-automation the scope session may change for a run: specs, page objects and fixtures. Changes are temporary. They are saved as artifacts/local-tests/temporary-changes.patch, applied to a fresh worktree and never committed.
localTests._why_limits: A ceiling for the list, not a target. The scope session takes the specs that can see the change (a testid links them, or — at most 3 — their steps go through a screen the change touched), adds every impacted module's main-functionality specs (index.cjs mainSpecs: the module's smoke-tagged specs, at most 5, or its first 5 cases when it tags none), and never pads the list toward maxSpecs spec files or maxRunMinutes minutes with other module specs that cannot see the change (a dry run that padded to the cap picked 40 unrelated specs, about 37 minutes). A change no spec reaches gets NO test written or suggested: the modules' main-functionality specs are what runs, and QA add any other test themselves (`added <file>`). The list is never cut for the budget: when it is over, the whole list stays and the list QA approves says so, and the list runs in full if QA approves it. maxRunMinutes is also the deadline of EACH Cypress run (the ticket run, the retry of its failures, the re-run on the base code), so a list over it may not finish; unfinished specs are reported as not finished.
localTests._why_devApproval: UNUSED since the step left the Loop: nothing waits for a developer any more, because QA approves every local run before it starts and the results are recorded, not signed off. Still checked ('any' or 'all') because scripts/localtests.cjs reads this block field for field (settingsFrom, pinned to localTestsConfig() by src/lib/localtests-cli.test.ts); remove it together with that mirror.
localTests._why_failuresBlock: UNUSED since the step left the Loop: there is no MR left to hold back, so a finished run marks the ticket labels.localTestsDone whether its tests passed or failed, and a failure that does NOT also fail on the tested branch (dev or stage) is called out to the MR author in the results comment. Still checked (true or false) for the reason _why_devApproval gives.
localTests._why_releaseBranchPattern: Source branches that make an MR a branch PROMOTION, not a fix, so the readiness check (hooks/local-tests-ready.cjs) never takes a release merge for the ticket's change. Together with branches.protected: a 'stage → dev' MR that mentions a ticket is not the change that fixed it. Release branches are named Adhoc-YYYY-MM-DD. The hook compiles this source with the 'i' flag, so adhoc-… matches too. Moved here from the retired Ready For Automation mode's block, whose readiness check used the same rule.
localTests._why_targetBranches: The branches a ticket's own merge request may be merged into for its local automation tests to start. ERP fixes land on dev, and hotfixes straight on stage: both are tested, at the MR's merge commit on whichever branch it went into, and a failure is re-run on that same branch just before the merge. A promotion or a backmerge between them (stage → dev, dev → stage) is never the change (branches.protected and releaseBranchPattern), so a fix is tested once, where it landed. A ticket with own MRs merged into both has its latest merge tested and every one scoped, and the list names any MR merged into the other branch. Absent, branches.base alone. Read by hooks/local-tests-ready.cjs and through localTestsTargetBranches() (src/lib/config.ts); anything but a list of branch names holds every ticket, naming this field.

_comment_concurrency: In-flight TICKET cap. The old MUST-STAY-1 constraint is now carried by the promotion mutex (src/lib/promotion.ts): the deploy script ships the TIP of dev, so exactly one run may occupy the merge→deploy→qa window at a time — that is where attribution lives, and the mutex enforces it while every other phase pipelines freely. Residual cap reasons: worktrees symlink ONE shared node_modules/venv (a second webpack build during another run's verify contends on the babel cache), and the port pool (PORT_POOL, default 3) bounds server-holding phases. Raise toward the pool size once shared-cache contention is observed to be tolerable. Set to 1 deliberately: the operator runs one ticket per loop and scales by starting more conductors, so the fleet-wide ceiling is PORT_POOL and each process holds exactly one run — which also keeps the shared node_modules/venv contention this comment warns about at one build per conductor.
